info.title: Leviath HTTP API
info.description: The REST and WebSocket surface `lev serve` puts in front of the shared-world daemon. Every route requires a bearer token. Paths here are checked against the router in crates/leviath-cli/src/commands/serve/mod.rs by a test in that file, so a route added without a spec entry fails the build. See https://leviath.dev/docs/api.

get.description:
A minimal HTML page saying the server is running. **The only route that does not require the bearer token**, because it exists to be opened in a browser tab and a tab cannot send an `Authorization` header.

Its purpose is TLS, not status: with a self-signed certificate, opening this in a tab is how a user reaches the certificate interstitial and accepts it, after which a browser console's `fetch` to the same origin inherits the exception.

It deliberately reports nothing else - no version, no run counts, no endpoint list. Anyone who can load it already knows the port is open, and that should remain all they learn.

**Breaking change in 0.3.0**: returns the same paginated envelope as /api/runs rather than a bare array. Check `blueprints.envelope` in the `capabilities` list on GET /api/config.

Note that pagination saves the server nothing here - discovery parses every manifest on every request regardless of page size, and the catalog is bounded by what a person installs. `q` is the parameter with real value.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Larger values are clamped rather than refused.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous page's next_cursor. Opaque; bound to the query that minted it.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring over name, description and stage names.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Ordering key.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Ascending by name is the order a person reads a catalog in.

post.summary: Install a blueprint from a manifest string
Validate a manifest without installing it

200.description: The verdict. Note an invalid manifest is still a 200 with `valid: false`.

get.description: The catalog entry plus the manifest text, the context regions, and fan_outs: one entry per fan-out stage with its worker source, merge stage and both caps (max_workers, max_items) resolved as the daemon applies them, null meaning unlimited.

Supersedes the GET half of /api/agents, which returns every run ever recorded as one unbounded array.

Pagination is keyset, not offset: runs are created and deleted while a client walks the list, and an offset into a shifting list silently skips and repeats items. Pass `next_cursor` back verbatim and loop until it is null.

`sort=started_at` is the only immutable sort key, and it is the default. `updated_at` also advances on the daemon's 30-second persistence heartbeat, so every live run moves under a walk, and a run whose sort value changes mid-walk may be skipped or repeated. Use started_at for a stable walk, and `since=` with no cursor to poll for what changed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Larger values are clamped rather than refused; the live cap is in GET /api/config.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from a previous page's next_cursor. Opaque - do not parse or construct it. Presenting one against a different sort, order or filter set is a 400, not a quietly different result.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses to keep. Matched loosely: waiting_input, waitinginput and Waiting-Input are all accepted.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Which runs to list by their place in the tree. `none` keeps only runs nobody started, which is what a top-level list wants; a run id keeps that run's direct children. Omitted lists every run, sub-agents included. A run id that names nothing gives an empty page rather than a 404. Announced as `runs.parent`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Ordering key. last_progress_at falls back to started_at where it is absent.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring to search for. Not a regex; no boolean operators or phrase quoting, and ASCII case folding only.

parameters.name: q_in
parameters.description: Comma-separated search sources: meta, files, context, logs, journal. The last three read files, so they are opt-in and subject to a scan cap - see scan_truncated in the response. They also match the raw JSON on disk, so a query containing a quote, backslash or newline may not match text that does contain it.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated top-level RunMeta fields to return. run_id is always included. Nested paths are not supported.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated run ids to fetch directly, bypassing the scan. Cannot be combined with cursor, q, status or since. Ids that no longer exist come back in `missing` rather than failing the request.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Keep only runs whose sort field is at or after this unix-seconds value. Inclusive, so a client polling with the previous response's server_time re-receives same-second items rather than losing them.

delete.description:
Prunes finished runs. The realistic use is "clear everything older than a month", which one request per run over a few hundred runs does badly.

Needs `before` or `ids`. Neither is a 400 rather than "every run": a bulk delete with no predicate is far more likely to be a client that failed to build its query than an operator asking to erase the machine's history.

Partial success is the normal outcome, not a failure. A sweep that meets a live run has still correctly deleted the rest, so this answers 200 with a verdict per run rather than failing the whole request. Read `skipped` to find out why the list did not empty. Use DELETE /api/runs/{id} when you want a status code per outcome.

Every run named takes its sub-agent tree with it, as on the single-run route, so `deleted` can hold ids you never mentioned. Reporting them is the point: they are the runs that are now gone.

Deletion is real and irreversible: the run directory and its transcript go.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Delete every finished run whose updated_at is strictly before this unix timestamp. Ignored when ids is given.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated run ids to delete. At most max_ids (see GET /api/config) per request.

200.description: The sweep ran. Every named run is in exactly one of the two lists.

delete.description:
Removes a finished run's directory from disk. Distinct from DELETE /api/agents/{id}, which cancels the run and leaves the record: one stops the work, the other forgets it happened.

Deletion is real and irreversible - the directory and everything in it, including the transcript. A console offering a "Delete" that only hid the run locally would tell somebody clearing a sensitive transcript that it was gone when it was not.

The run's sub-agent runs go with it. A fan-out worker or a sub_agent spawn is drawn nested under the run that started it and nothing else on disk accounts for it, so a delete that left them behind did not merely strand them: a client that nests runs under their parent has nowhere to draw a parentless run but the top level, and the delete read as a promotion. The walk is downwards only - deleting a sub-agent run leaves its parent and its siblings exactly where they were.

409 on a live run: removing a directory out from under a running agent is a different and much larger feature, so cancel it first. A live sub-agent is a 409 too, and the reason names it. 404 on a run that is already gone, so a client that lost the response to its own delete can repeat it rather than treat a missing run as a failure. 409 as well on a run whose record will not parse, which force=true overrides.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The run id.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Delete a run whose meta.json will not parse, which is otherwise a 409. A record that cannot be read is not proof the run finished - that is what a live run looks like to a binary whose RunMeta has moved on - so this is something the caller types rather than the default. The bulk route never forces.

get.description: Deprecated: use GET /api/runs, which paginates and supports search. This route returns every run ever recorded as one array, and is kept unchanged for existing clients.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to one status.

post.description: Returns as soon as the daemon accepts the run. Poll GET /api/agents/{id} or subscribe to /ws for what happens next.

get.summary: One run's metadata, with secrets redacted
How the context window changed over the run
get.description:
**Breaking change in 0.3.0**: paginated, returning the shared envelope rather than every recorded point as one array. Each point carries a full context window with untruncated region text, on a journal that grows for as long as the run does, so the unpaged form was comfortably the largest response in the API.

The cursor is the point index. The journal is append-only, so an index is stable once written and new points only ever arrive at the end.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Points per page. Capped lower than the run listing because each item carries a whole context window.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation token from the previous page's next_cursor.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` is chronological, and matches what the unpaged response gave. `desc` starts from the most recent point, which is what a view tailing a live run wants.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Byte offset to start reading at. An offset landing mid-character is moved forward to the next boundary, and the response's `offset` says where the window actually began, so concatenating pages reproduces the file. Past the end returns 416.

get.summary: Read a file inside the run's workdir, or list files
get.description:
With `path`, reads that file: confined to the run's working directory, 1 MiB per request. A larger file is read a window at a time - pass `offset` and continue from the `next_offset` each response carries, which is how an agent's dataset artifact is fetched in full. Without `path`, lists instead, and the response carries `kind: "listing"` so the two shapes can be told apart. Reading a file returns exactly the shape it always has.

`source=modified` lists what the run recorded changing - free, but capped when it was recorded, so check `modified_files_truncated`. `source=workdir` reads the filesystem, **one directory level per request**; pass a directory as `path` to descend. Note `modifying_tool_calls` counts modifying tool calls and not distinct files, so subtracting it from the entry count does not give "how many more files".

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Workdir-relative path. A file is read; a directory is listed; absent lists the run's files.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `modified` lists what the run recorded changing; `workdir` reads one directory level of the filesystem.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include dot-prefixed entries when listing a directory.

get.description: A run's logs, by stage. Output is recorded per stage under stages/<idx>/, and the two streams are kept separate rather than interleaved because they share no ordering.

parameters.name: tail
parameters.description: Return only the last N bytes (not lines).

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage index to read, or `all` to join every stage oldest first. Defaults to the stage the run is on now.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: `output` for the assistant's readable output, `logs` for the operational stream: tool calls, token counts and errors.

get.summary: The run's output and token usage

200.description: The result so far. Check `status` before trusting `output`.

get.summary: Token roll-ups across this run and its descendants

post.summary: Pause a run after its in-flight step
Inject a message into a running agent's context

get.summary: The question this run is waiting on, if any

post.description: Body: `request_id` (the open request's id) plus one of `value`, `choice_index`, or `approved` with an optional `scope` (`once`, `stage`, `session`). A deny (`approved: false`) may carry `feedback`, a string the model reads inside the tool result for the refused call: `[denied] User declined tool call '<tool>'. Feedback: <text>`. `feedback` beside `approved: true` is a 400. 202 once the daemon holds the answer, 404 when nothing with that id is open. Announced as `interaction.feedback`.
Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed, because adding a stdio server is arbitrary code execution by construction.

post.summary: Begin the OAuth flow for this server, or report that it needs no login
post.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed, because it opens the operator's browser on the host running the server and completes an OAuth flow there. Returns `{"status": "authenticated"}` when the browser flow completed and credentials were stored, or `{"status": "not_required"}` when the server answered a probe carrying its configured headers, which means there is no OAuth flow to run.

post.summary: Connect and list this server's tools
post.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed, because it connects to the server and, for a stdio server, spawns its configured command.

get.summary: The offline `lev doctor` checks, as data
get.description: The same checks as `lev doctor --offline`: config, search and resolve, then stop. Nothing here contacts a provider or the daemon, so pressing the button costs nothing. A failing check is reported inside a 200 with `ok: false`, not as an HTTP error: the request succeeded, the install is what did not.

post.summary: The whole `lev doctor` chain, billed calls included
post.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed: past the offline checks it makes one billed provider call, then spawns a throwaway one-stage run through the daemon (a second billed call) and waits for it. One at a time; a second caller while one is going gets 409. A failing check is reported inside a 200 with `ok: false`, not as an HTTP error.

409.description: Another live doctor run is already in progress

get.summary: How this copy was installed, and what upgrades it
get.description: The same answer `lev update --check --json` prints, from the same planner, so a client never sends a user a command their own terminal disagrees with. `install_method` is one of `homebrew`, `scoop`, `cargo`, `script`, `unknown`. `binary.action` is `run` with a `commands` list of argv lists to run in order, or `advise` with a `message` to show. Read-only and available without `--allow-admin`: it works out what an update would do and does none of it.

post.summary: Carry out the update the GET half describes
post.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed, because it runs a package manager, rewrites the agents directory and rewrites the config. Answers 202 with a `job_id` and runs the work behind it: an upgrade is a download and an install, so every step change is sent on `/ws` as `update_progress`, the last as `update_finished`, and `GET /api/update/jobs/{id}` answers the same record for a client that would rather poll. The body names which parts to do - `binary`, `agents`, `migrations`, each defaulting to true, so an empty body is the whole plan. A `binary.action` of `advise` stays advice: the step is recorded as `advised` with the reason and no compile is started. A blueprint you edited locally is never installed. 409 while another update is running.

get.summary: Where one update run got to
get.description: Admin only, mounted alongside `POST /api/update`. The same record the `update_finished` frame carries: `status` of `running`, `complete` or `failed`; a `steps` list with one entry per step (`binary`, `agents`, `migrations`), each `pending`, `running`, `done`, `skipped`, `advised` or `failed` with a line of detail; and `restart_required`, set when the binary was replaced - this server and the daemon keep running the old build until they are restarted. The last few runs are kept, so a client that reads back after the fact finds the job.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: An update job id, as returned by POST /api/update.

get.summary: One directory level, for a folder picker

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Include dot-directories.

post.summary: Create one directory, for a folder picker's New Folder

path.description: Absolute parent directory. Must exist, and lie inside --workdir-root when one is set.

name.description: The new directory's name: one segment, no separators, not . or ..

get.summary: The active configuration, with credentials redacted

put.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed.

200.description: Whether the key and value are usable.

post.summary: Ask an OpenAI-compatible server what models it serves
post.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed. Body: `base_url` (required), `api_key`, `headers`. Answers `{"models": [ids]}`, or 502 carrying the server's own error text, or 400 for a base URL with no scheme.

get.description: A WebSocket upgrade, not a JSON response. Authenticate with `?token=` since a browser cannot set a header on the handshake. Each frame is a ServerEvent.
As /ws, filtered to a single run.

What each stage spent, in tokens and in dollars, per visit as well as in total, and which regions it carried. Not derivable from the other routes: a stage that ran and wrote nothing to any region leaves no trace in context/history, so `entered` is the only way to tell it from a stage that was never reached, and pricing is the daemon's job - a console multiplying tokens by a rate card of its own produces a fourth answer that disagrees with the run's, the stage's and the provider's.

200.description: Stage records in blueprint order. Empty for a run that has not reached its first stage boundary.

get.summary: Tools an agent on this machine can call
get.description: Built-ins, sub-agent tools, the named agent's own `tools/*.rhai` and the global ones, each with a `source`. `skipped` carries the `.rhai` files that were found and could not be offered, with the reason. MCP tools are not included; `/api/mcp/servers/{name}` answers for those.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Scope to this agent's own directory.

get.summary: Rhai scripts this scope can see
get.description: Script tools from the agent's `tools/` and the global directory, the region hooks, stage hooks and output validators the agent's manifest declares, and the model providers in `~/.leviath/providers`. Each entry carries its kind, its source (`agent` or `global`) and whether it compiles right now; a provider also carries a `provider` object with what its `// @` annotations declare. Providers are listed with or without `agent`, since nothing scopes one to an agent.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Scope to this agent's own directory.

post.summary: Compile a script without writing it
post.description: Takes `kind` and `content`, plus `hooks` for a stage hook, and answers with `valid` and the compiler's complaint. Writes nothing and runs nothing: every compiler here stops at the AST, a provider's `initialize` included. A provider that does not define `initialize(config)` and `inference(state, request)` fails here rather than at the first inference.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name without its `.rhai` extension.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Scope to this agent's own directory. A `provider` is global to the machine and refuses this parameter.

put.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed, because a `.rhai` file is executable code every agent then runs. A file that does not compile is still written, and the response says so.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name without its `.rhai` extension.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Scope to this agent's own directory. A `provider` is global to the machine and refuses this parameter.

delete.description: Admin only. Mounted only when `lev serve --allow-admin` is passed.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name without its `.rhai` extension.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Scope to this agent's own directory. A `provider` is global to the machine and refuses this parameter.

bearerAuth.description: The token from `lev serve --token` or LEVIATH_API_TOKEN. The server refuses to start without one. WebSocket routes take it as `?token=` instead.

Id.name: id
Id.description: A run id, as returned by `lev run --json` or POST /api/agents.

blueprint.description: An installed blueprint name, or a path to one.

yolo.description: Run unattended. Refused when the server was started with --no-remote-yolo.

workdir.description: Confined to --workdir-root when the server sets one.

regions.description: Seed content per named context region.

output_format.description: Ask for the final output in this shape, overriding the blueprint's. Any label works - nothing converts between shapes; the label reaches the model, which produces the bytes. Naming this without output_schema drops a schema the blueprint declared.

output_instructions.description: Extra guidance about that shape. How an unusual format gets explained.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema the final output must satisfy. The only thing that inspects the answer's contents, and only because you asked: a failing submission is refused back to the agent to correct.

callback_secret.description: Shared secret for the HMAC-SHA256 signature on that callback.

status.description: The run's status, in the same words a run object uses: starting, running, waiting_input, paused, complete, complete_interactive, error, cancelled. A server that does not announce `events.run_status` sends the Display spelling here instead (`WaitingInput`).

output.description: The tail of the last stage's log: what the run did. Prefer final_output for what it concluded.

final_output.description: The answer the agent submitted, if any.

FinalOutput.description: What an agent handed back. `content` is byte-for-byte what it submitted; nothing re-serializes it. `format` is an opaque label the server never interprets - match on it to decide how to render.

format.description: Whatever shape was asked for: "markdown", "json", "a2ui", a media type, anything. Not a closed set.

truncated.description: The answer hit the 256 KiB cap and was cut short.

artifacts.description: Files the run produced, as workdir-relative paths. An answer is one model response, so anything larger is a file named here. Fetch one with GET /api/agents/{id}/files?path=.

stages.description: One record per declared stage, in blueprint order.

index.description: Position in the blueprint's stage list. Not a progress measure: stages loop and revisit.

status.description: `skipped` means the run finished without ever entering this stage, which is distinct from `pending` (not yet, on a live run).

entered.description: Whether the run has ever been in this stage. Position cannot answer this - a graph reaches its stages in whatever order its edges describe. False for every stage of a run recorded before Leviath tracked this, because the field is not in those files; read it together with `status`.

cache_write_tokens.description: Without this a stage showing no cache reads cannot be told apart from one paying to write a prefix nothing reuses.

cost_usd.description: What this stage spent, accumulated across revisits. Null means unknown, never free: some call was served by a model with no reported cost and no known rates, so any total would understate by an unknown amount. Counts every call made in the stage - its own turns, the compaction calls that summarize its context, and the routing call at its boundary. The run's title call belongs to no stage, so the stages can sum to slightly less than the run's own cost_usd. Absent on a daemon without the runs.stages.cost capability, which is not the same as null.

unpriced_calls.description: Calls in this stage that could not be priced at all. Non-zero forces cost_usd to null.

cost_is_exact.description: Whether every priced call carried the provider's own cost figure. False means the total is a reconstruction from published rates, not the invoice.

cost_priced_usd.description: The priced subtotal, kept even while cost_usd is null so a resumed run does not restart from zero. Not a substitute for cost_usd: showing it while calls went unpriced is the partial total that looks authoritative and is not.

visit_count.description: How many times the run has entered this stage, counting past the point where `visits` stopped recording them. Greater than visits.length means the per-visit split is partial and the accumulated figures on this record are the complete ones.

visits.description: Each contiguous stay in this stage, oldest first, capped at 128. The record itself accumulates across revisits, which is the right total for the stage and the wrong shape for a graph of the path a run took, where a stage entered twice is two nodes. A stage that loops back to itself starts a new visit; iterations within one stay do not. Empty on a stage the run never entered, and on records written before Leviath split visits out.

region_tokens.description: The largest each region reached while this stage was active, by region name. The number that decides whether a region is earning its place.

runaway_warned.description: The stage's per-call prompt passed four times its first call - the shape of a region accumulating without a cap.

started_at.description: Unix seconds; null until the stage is entered.

ended_at.description: Unix seconds; null until the stage is left.

active.description: How long this stage actually spent working, as against how long it was the cursor. Null on records written before Leviath kept the clock, which is distinct from a stage that did no work. A stage the run is parked in - paused, or holding a prompt open - is still the cursor stage, so started_at..ended_at counts time nothing spent working.

banked_secs.description: Seconds from spans that have already ended.

since.description: Unix seconds when the span in progress began, or null while the clock is stopped. The working total is banked_secs plus now - since when since is set.

StageVisitRecord.description: One contiguous stay in a stage: what it cost, and how long it took. The nodes of the graph a run actually walked, where a stage entered twice is two of them.

entered_at.description: Unix seconds when the run entered the stage on this visit.

left_at.description: Unix seconds when it left. Null on the visit in progress, which is the last entry of the stage the run is in right now.

cost_usd.description: What this visit spent. Null means unknown, never free, on the same rule as the stage and the run.

unpriced_calls.description: Calls in this visit that could not be priced at all. Non-zero forces cost_usd to null.

cost_is_exact.description: Whether every priced call in this visit carried the provider's own cost figure rather than one computed from published rates.

cost_priced_usd.description: The priced subtotal, kept even while cost_usd is null so a resumed run does not restart this visit's accounting from zero.

active.description: How long this visit actually spent working, as against how long the run was parked in the stage. Same shape and same rule as the stage's own clock.

banked_secs.description: Seconds from spans that have already ended.

since.description: Unix seconds when the span in progress began, or null while the clock is stopped.

id.description: The run that was not deleted.

reason.description: Why, as a sentence a console can show verbatim.

skipped.description: Ids that were left alone, each with a reason. A live run and a run that was already gone are both non-deletions, and a caller needs to tell them apart.
